html:
The Annan Plan was a United Nations proposal to reunite Cyprus as a federation of two states, put to separate referendums on 24 April 2004. Turkish Cypriots voted yes by about two to one; Greek Cypriots voted no by about three to one.

Named after the UN Secretary General Kofi Annan, it set out a loose union, limits on the return of refugees and property, and a reduced Turkish troop presence. Greek Cypriot leaders said it gave too much to the Turkish side. A week later Cyprus joined the European Union still divided, with EU law suspended in the north. The vote left the division in place. Crossings through the Green Line had opened a year before.
sum: The Annan Plan was a United Nations proposal to reunite Cyprus as a federation of two states, put to separate referendums on 24 April 2004. Turkish Cypriots voted yes by about two to one; Greek Cypriots voted no by about three to one.
